what_it_does: IoT wireless transmitters typically need a crystal oscillator (a quartz resonator) to maintain a stable radio frequency—but crystals add cost, power, and size. This paper describes a crystal-free FM transmitter that uses a free-running oscillator (no crystal needed) but compensates for its natural drift and noise using a neural network. The network learns a modulation and coding scheme that adapts the transmitted signal in real time to account for oscillator imperfections, maintaining reliable communication despite the inherent jitter. This trades the cost of a crystal for the cost of a small neural network, potentially enabling cheaper, smaller IoT radios.
